lede: Get to know a little about me and the work I do.
body:
Marcia Gomezcoello González was born in the city of Azogues, Ecuador. She attended secondary school at the Colegio Manuela Garaicoa de Calderón in Cuenca, Ecuador, and completed her higher education at the State University of Cuenca, earning the degree of «Doctor of Medicine and Surgery». She also studied elder care.
Born into a family of artists, she inherited a passion for art, music and literature. She is a writer, poet, graphic designer, cultural promoter, volunteer crochet workshop instructor, video creator and producer, singer and composer.
She wrote her first short story at the age of eleven. She has written more than a hundred unpublished songs, both lyrics and music, five of which have been arranged and recorded. One of them was recorded at the Opus Ethica studios and can be heard today on YouTube under the title «Corazón Valiente» — a song created and dedicated to sick children when a donation of crocheted garments was made, after she gave free workshops to women of the Corona community in Queens, NY.
She is the founder, creator, organizer and promoter of Tardes Literarias y Artísticas NY (TARLITEART), and creates the videos and promotion for these events, which have been held from January 2019 to the present. They present, support and promote writers, poets, painters, singers, dancers and artists of every kind. The program takes place on the last Saturday of each month at the Corona Library in Queens, NY, as a non-profit event, where she works as a library volunteer.
She has two YouTube channels: a crochet channel, «Marcia Gomezcoello Creations», with more than 173,000 subscribers, for which she received a recognition plaque from YouTube.
And a two-needle knitting channel, «Knitting with Marcia Gomezcoello», with more than 88,000 subscribers. She loves to make knitting a true art, and made giant flowers for the Queens Museum, NY, which have decorated several of its events, as well as for the flower festival held in Queens.
She is a member of the Confederation of Ecuadorian Journalists in NY.
She has taken part in many book fairs and literary events in New York City.
_guiaAlbum: EL ÁLBUM: las fotos de su vida. Cada bloque de 'items' es una foto pegada en la hoja del álbum, sujeta por cuatro esquineros de papel. Para añadir una, copiar un bloque entero y cambiarle los valores: no hay tope, y el orden de la lista es el orden en la hoja — conviene ponerlas de la más antigua a la más reciente. 'photo' es el nombre del archivo puesto en public/content/; 'pie' es la línea que va debajo (dónde fue, quiénes salen) y puede quedar vacía; 'year' es el año, que sale en dorado sobre el pie y también puede quedar vacío. 'shape' es la forma de la foto —'cuadrado', 'alto' (más alta que ancha) o 'ancho' (más ancha que alta)—, las mismas tres de todo el sitio: aquí todas las fotos salen del mismo alto y cada una ocupa el ancho que le toca por su forma, así que mezclarlas es justamente lo que hace que la hoja se vea armada a mano. Para quitar la sección entera, dejar 'items': []

items.title: LAIA International Short Story Award
items.text: Winner of the LAIA International short story contest. Her story was included in an anthology on the theme «Journeys».

items.title: 2 YouTube channels

recognition._guia: Premios, menciones y participaciones. Cada bloque lleva 'year', 'title', 'text', 'photo' y 'shape' — la foto puede ser el diploma, la placa o una foto de la entrega, y 'shape' es la forma del marco: 'cuadrado', 'alto' (más alto que ancho) o 'ancho' (más ancho que alto) — las mismas tres formas que se usan en todo el sitio. La foto de arriba, la del diploma, también lleva su 'shape'. Sin foto sale un marco de reserva. Para añadir otro, copiar un bloque entero.
